title: Number Quest Unit 1 · The Counting House (Explorer)

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 7,304?
misconceptions: read the 7 one place too small
read the 7 two places too small
read the 7 as just 7 and forgot its place
items.why: The 7 sits in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands: 7,000. Where a digit sits decides what it is worth.

items.q: Which choice shows 4,058 in expanded form?
misconceptions: read the tens digit as hundreds
wrote the digits without their place values
items.why: 4,058 has 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 5 tens and 8 ones. That is 4,000 + 50 + 8. The 0 says there are no hundreds to write.

misconceptions: compared the ones digits instead of the tens
gave up before comparing place by place
items.why: Compare place by place from the left. The thousands and hundreds match, then the tens differ: 2 tens beats 1 ten, so 3,921 is greater.

items.q: What is 463 rounded to the nearest ten?
misconceptions: rounded up even though the ones digit is 3
rounded down to a hundred instead of to a ten
rounded to the nearest hundred, not the nearest ten
items.why: 463 sits between 460 and 470. The ones digit is 3, less than 5, so it rounds down to 460.

items.q: What is 1,450 rounded to the nearest hundred?
misconceptions: rounded down when the tens digit was 5
rounded to the nearest thousand, not hundred
kept the number and forgot to round
items.why: To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit. It is 5, and 5 or more rounds up, so 1,450 becomes 1,500.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 398 + 204?
misconceptions: worked out the exact sum instead of an estimate
items.why: 398 is about 400 and 204 is about 200, so the sum is about 400 + 200 = 600. An estimate uses friendly numbers, not the exact sum.

misconceptions: added 1 instead of following the rule
items.why: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 7, 12, 17, 22. Keep the add-5 rule and the next one is 22 + 5 = 27.

items.q: A pattern starts at 2 and follows the rule add 6. What is the fourth number?
items.why: Start at 2 and add 6 for each new number: 2, 8, 14, 20. The fourth number is 20.

items.q: Which sum shows the pattern even + even = even?
misconceptions: picked an even and an odd number
items.why: 2 and 6 are both even, and their sum, 8, is even too. Each of the other sums uses at least one odd number.
